name: plan-eng-review
conclusion_quantitative: plan-eng-review (Act) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 6 autonomy limits, 10+ clarification rules, 10+ approval gates, 1 validation rule, 10+ escalation rules. Strongest: clarification rules.
conclusion_qualitative: plan-eng-review (in its pstack version) reviews an implementation plan like an engineering manager (architecture, code quality, test coverage and performance) before code is written. Most of its rules make the agent consult the user, one question per issue, and it needs explicit approval before acting on another AI model's advice, starting other skills or upgrading. It works with a fixed tool set and flags rather than fixes problems in shared repositories. It requires evidence before calling work done, and stops and escalates after repeated failures, on security doubts, or when it cannot verify the work.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 6 autonomy limits (6 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly prose.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 6 rules, all strict, 2 tied to a situation, mostly running text. The front matter limits the agent to `Read`, `Write`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `AskUserQuestion`, `Bash` and `WebSearch`. When proactive mode is off it runs only the skills the user types, and in shared repositories it flags problems instead of fixing them. It moves on without asking when the scope check finds nothing overbuilt, and adds a regression test to the plan without asking whenever it finds a regression.

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ clarification rules (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly prose.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), all strict, 2 tied to a situation, mostly running text. The agent asks the user about proactive behavior during setup, says exactly what it needs when information is missing, and asks for the user's input on every issue instead of assuming a direction. When the plan looks overbuilt it asks whether to reduce scope; after each review section it stops and asks one question per issue; and it asks about each disagreement with the outside AI reviewer and each possible TODO.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ approval gates (9 mandatory, 1 advisory; 4 conditional), mostly prose.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), 9 strict and 1 only a suggestion (worded with "might"), 4 tied to a situation, all in running text. validation.conclusion_quantitative: 1 validation rule (1 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There is one strict rule, always on, in a bullet point. A task counts as done only when every step is complete with evidence for each claim.

statements.quote: **DONE** — All steps completed successfully. Evidence provided for each claim.

escalation.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ escalation rules (8 mandatory, 2 advisory; 5 conditional), mostly list.
escalation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), 8 strict and 2 counted as suggestions (they contain "should" and, in a quoted message, "could"), 5 tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The agent flags anything that looks wrong and reports concerns or blockers. It must stop and escalate after 3 failed attempts, on doubts about a security-sensitive change, or when it cannot verify the work. When a needed skill file, web search or the outside reviewer's login fails, it tells the user and carries on.

statements.quote: Always flag anything that looks wrong — one sentence, what you noticed and its impact.
**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS** — Completed, but with issues the user should know about. List each concern.
**BLOCKED** — Cannot proceed. State what is blocking and what was tried.
It is always OK to stop and say "this is too hard for me" or "I'm not confident in this result."
If you have attempted a task 3 times without success, STOP and escalate.
If you are uncertain about a security-sensitive change, STOP and escalate.
If the scope of work exceeds what you can verify, STOP and escalate.
If the Read fails (file not found), say: "Could not load /validate — proceeding with standard review."
If WebSearch is unavailable, skip this check and note: "Search unavailable — proceeding with in-distribution knowledge only."
Auth failure (stderr contains "auth", "login", "unauthorized"): "Codex auth failed. Run \`codex login\` to authenticate."
